title: Forfeitable "security deposit" for data-entry work vs. contract data-entry project with quality checks
summary: A job seeker calls the number on a NaukriHub listing for home-based data-entry work posted under TalentBridge Staffing. In the fraud case, the coordinator says work files are released only after a "refundable security deposit", which the contract says is forfeited if accuracy falls below a threshold. In the legitimate case, the coordinator explains the same accuracy standard, an NDA, and quality checks, and states that low accuracy means rework or removal from the project, never a charge or deposit.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a homemaker, student, or retiree seeking home-based work; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Work: typing scanned forms into a spreadsheet, about 3–4 hours a day, paid per completed batch, stated as [AMOUNT_1] (₹8,000–₹20,000 per month).
Both coordinators mention an "agreement", a "security" requirement, and a 95% accuracy target.
Channel: the recipient places the call. Turn 1 is the coordinator answering.

fraud.label_rationale: The worker must pay money in before receiving work, and the terms are set up so the money is kept by claiming accuracy failures.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the deposit, then keep it by declaring the work below standard (and possibly demand "penalty" payments).
stable_facts: Deposit: [AMOUNT_2] (₹2,000–₹8,000), called "refundable security deposit" against "data confidentiality".
Paid to [UPI_ID_1] before the login and first batch are issued.
The agreement says the deposit is forfeited if accuracy is below 95%.
The coordinator describes the deposit as "standard for all home-based projects".

Below-target accuracy means the batch is returned for correction; repeated failure means removal from the project.
Security" means data security: no downloading or sharing files, work only in the browser portal https://work.talentbridge.invalid.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud coordinator may lower the deposit, offer a "discount", or stress refundability. They must not switch to OTPs, remote access, or pay-to-unlock tasks (that is jr_02). The legitimate coordinator must not introduce any payment or penalty after the branch.

must_preserve: work description, hours, pay, and 95% target identical across cases
_F deposit before login with forfeiture clause at turn 7
_L explicit no-deposit statement and non-monetary quality consequences
may_vary: form type (insurance forms, survey sheets, invoices)

ambiguities: Security", "agreement", and "accuracy" appear in both cases; none is evidence.
Distinct from jr_01: here there is no placement or job guarantee; the payment is collateral against the recipient's own work output, with a built-in forfeiture condition.
Distinct from jr_02: jr_02 pays small commissions then asks for repeated deposits to unlock earnings; here there is one deposit before any work, recovered through an accuracy clause.
The recipient initiating the call does not make _F less of a fraud attempt.

evidence_references.claim: Upfront payment and denied withdrawals are red flags in fake job schemes (C11)
Fake recruiters ask job seekers to pay in advance for "verification & registration" (CJ09)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
